hooks.name: entity_ignite
hooks.neoforge: none (NeoForge has no ignition event; Bukkit's EntityCombustEvent)

rust_summary: an entity a cause sets alight, of the entity's `kind`, with that cause (`native_entity_ignite`).
doc_summary: `native_entity_ignite(entity, kind, cause, ticks, canceled)` is asked when a cause is about to set the entity `entity` of type `kind` (`minecraft:player`, `minecraft:zombie`, `minecraft:armor_stand`) alight for `ticks` fire ticks: `cause` is `fire_aspect` (Fire Aspect and the other attack enchantments), `flame_arrow` (a burning arrow hitting its target), `projectile` (a blaze's or a fire charge's small fireball), `lightning` (a bolt's 8 seconds), `lava` (standing in lava or in a lava cauldron), `fire_block` (standing in fire, a boat in fire or on a burning block, or an armor stand set alight by fire or campfire damage), `sun` (sunlight burning an undead), or `other` (a burning zombie's blow, which is no enchantment). `ticks` starts as the fire ticks the cause asks for and a mod may change it: the entity then burns for the ticks it left (0 to 72000, an hour; anything else is clamped), and 0 leaves it cold. `original_ticks` keeps the requested value, and is read-only: a write to it is ignored. Set `canceled` and it does not catch fire: the ignition is skipped, as if that cause had not applied, and a cancel wins over a changed `ticks`. Told for each of those causes the game itself applies, and for the player standing in lava, in a fire block or in a lava cauldron, every tick of the attempt, on the server's copy only: only a server's copy ignites, so only it is told, and a client's predicted tick (the window's own player) never is. Not yet told, and coming in later steps: a mob in lava, fire or sunlight; an arrow or another projectile in fire or lava; a dropped item in fire or lava; an armor stand merely standing in fire, whose own tick sets the fire; and an arrow set alight before it joins the level (which has no ID to name). Server-side. Bundles need "hooks": @API:entity_ignite@.
